result.summary: A single fragment from the Life of Homer reports that Homer, sitting in a tanner's yard, recited to an audience his Expedition of Amphiarus to Thebes and his Hymns to the Gods. It is only a testimony about the lost epic, not the poem itself.

scenes.title: Homer recites in the tanner's yard
scenes.summary: Homer sits in a tanner's yard and recites his poetry, including the Expedition of Amphiarus to Thebes and the Hymns, to those present.

characters.name: Homer
characters.description: the poet who recites his verses in the tanner's yard

characters.name: Amphiarus
characters.description: hero whose expedition to Thebes is the subject of a poem

analysis.text: The fragment comes from the ancient biography of Homer, which attributed to him poems now lost or assigned to others. It shows how the Expedition of Amphiarus was once counted among Homer's works.
The passage pictures the poet as a wandering performer whose epics and hymns were recited aloud to ordinary listeners in humble settings.

fun_facts.text: The Life of Homer attributed to Herodotus is not actually by Herodotus; its biographical details are largely legendary.

language_notes.text: The Expedition of Amphiarus to Thebes is the story of the seer Amphiarus, who joined the Seven against Thebes and was swallowed by the earth. It is attributed to Homer here but is now lost.
Fragment #1 means this line is a surviving quotation, taken from the Life of Homer, a biography once wrongly attributed to Herodotus (hence 'Pseudo-').

context_notes.text: The Life of Homer is a legendary biography. It shows Homer as a poor wandering poet who recites for hospitality among ordinary craftsmen, such as this tanner.
